# THE DRAW

*The cube casts three. A second caster, standing beside the wheel, doing the
same work by a different mechanism.*

## I · WHAT IT IS

One living cube holds the whole deck as a manifold, and a cast lifts three
cells out of it into the three houses. The three that rise are the reading.

This is not an early Wayfinder, and the distinction is worth stating plainly
because the two surfaces look alike in their output. The Wayfinder is a wheel:
it turns and settles, and its machinery is the ring, the skin and the voices.
The Draw is a cube: it holds the deck as a solid and lifts from it. They share
the canon and share nothing else, and either could be retired without touching
the other.

## II · WHY TWO CASTERS IS A QUESTION

Two mechanisms that produce the same kind of reading is either a richness or a
fork, and which one it is has not been decided.

The argument for keeping both: they teach different things. A wheel teaches
that the deck is a closed count that comes round. A cube teaches that the deck
is a body with an inside, and that a reading is three cells lifted out of a
whole that stays whole. Those are two true things about the same twenty-seven.

The argument against: a person meeting the system twice, in two rooms, with two
mechanisms, learns that the system has no single way of doing this. The
Aleatory Law does not forbid two casters, but the practice is easier to hold
when there is one door.

## III · WHAT IT ASKS

What to do with it. The architect has said it is interesting and that he is not
sure, and grouped it with the emergence, which is a fair grouping: both are
mechanisms in search of a home rather than pages in search of a ruling.

The available answers are that it folds into the living cube, which already
owns the cube's rite and would make this its cast; that it takes a room as a
second and deliberate caster; or that it is struck and the wheel stands alone.

## V · PROVENANCE

*Built as a prototype for the architect's eye during the redesign arc and left
unlinked. This chart entered the room on 19 July 2026, when the workings were
given a shelf. Its account of the difference between the two casters comes from
the surfaces' own imports, which is checkable: the Draw takes the cube engine,
the Wayfinder takes the wheel's. The weighing in section II is this chart's own
and is offered as an argument on both sides rather than a recommendation.
Nothing here predicts, and nothing here prescribes.*
